follow-up time: Variable, from diagnosis to end of pregnancy (median 13 days, range 2-159 days)
outcome: Doppler abnormalities (UA, MCA, DV, CPR, UtA)
cohort: 89 singleton fetuses diagnosed with UAT and with at least one Doppler evaluation before the end of pregnancy, compared to a GA-matched control group of normal fetuses
finding: Singleton fetuses with UAT experience significant hemodynamic changes, particularly increased UA-EDV and lower UA-PI and UA-RI, and have a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including stillbirth, IUGR, and NICU admission.
